0.long_answer: Lamotrigine is an anticonvulsant and mood-stabilizing medication that works primarily as a sodium channel blocker. Originally discovered in Switzerland, it is widely used in the treatment of epilepsy and bipolar disorder. One of the serious potential adverse effects of lamotrigine is the development of cutaneous adverse drug reactions, including Stevens–Johnson syndrome and its more severe form, toxic epidermal necrolysis (commonly known as Lyell's syndrome). Health care providers must monitor patients closely, particularly during the initiation of therapy, due to the risk of these potentially life‐threatening skin reactions.
